title: nexus ACP adapter v4: Nexus's subset of the Agent Client Protocol
description: Generated from AcpAdapterDocument in cli/src/acp/types.ts by cli/scripts/gen_acp_schema.mjs. Do not edit by hand. One line of an ACP connection to Nexus (newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0), in either direction: a message a client may send that Nexus acts on (AcpClientMessage), or a message Nexus sends (AcpAgentMessage). This is NOT the schema of the Agent Client Protocol: it describes only the subset of ACP version 1 that Nexus implements, plus Nexus's own extension methods (`_nexus/receipt/get`, `_nexus/verify`) and its `_meta` members (`nexus/...`). A valid ACP message outside this subset is answered with an error or ignored. Experimental: names and fields may change.

AcpAdapterDocument.description: One line of the connection, in either direction: the root of the published schema.

AcpAgentCapabilities.description: No `sessionCapabilities`: Nexus offers no session list, resume, fork, close or delete.

AcpClientError.description: The error member of a response a client sends to an agent request.

AcpDiffInfo.description: What Nexus knows about a diff beyond its text. `truncated`: the blocks come from a bounded preview or a cut diff.

AcpErrorData.description: Details of an error, in the standard `data` member (`_meta` is not allowed on a JSON-RPC error).

reason.description: A stable word for the cause, for example a sidecar error code or `sidecar_start_failed`.

AcpErrorResponse.description: `id` is null when the request's id could not be read (not JSON, too deep, too long, a batch).

AcpHistoryExtent.description: Conversation entries replayed on load, and how many the session holds.

AcpId.description: A JSON-RPC request id: a string or an integer.

AcpInitializeParams.description: `clientCapabilities` is accepted and never consulted: Nexus calls no client method (`fs/*`, `terminal/*`) whatever it says.

authMethods.description: Always empty: Nexus has no authentication method over ACP.

additionalDirectories.description: Accepted only when empty or null.

AcpLoadSessionResult.description: The specification's `session/load` response is an empty object; Nexus's own data is under `_meta`.

AcpMcpServersIgnored.description: Client-supplied MCP servers that were not connected: how many, and the sanitised names of the first of them.

AcpMeta.description: Custom data. Never read for authority: no `_meta` member a client sends changes what a session may do.

AcpNewSessionParams.description:
`mcpServers` is required by the specification and must be an array; its entries are not connected (see
ACP_DEVIATION_NO_CLIENT_MCP_SERVERS). `additionalDirectories` is accepted only when empty, and `systemPrompt` is
refused when present: Nexus supports neither.

additionalDirectories.description: Accepted only when empty or null.

AcpPermissionErrorResponse.description: An error answer to `session/request_permission`: a denial.

AcpPermissionRequest.description: `id` is an integer from a random start, so a reply sent before the request exists matches nothing.

AcpPermissionResponse.description: The client's answer to `session/request_permission`; `id` is the integer id of that request.

AcpPermissionResult.description: Only `selected` with the allow-once option id approves; every other result, well-formed or not, denies.

nexus/approval_digest.description: SHA-256 of the canonical `{tool, subject, preview, review}` of the approval this request asks about.

AcpPosture.description: The session's posture as the operator's machine set it. Reported, never set, over ACP.

AcpPromptBlock.description: The baseline content blocks (published specification, content). `image`, `audio` and `resource` need capabilities Nexus does not declare, and are refused.

AcpReceiptGetParams.description: Without `receiptId`: the latest receipt of the session.

AcpResourceLinkBlock.description: Reduced to one reference line of the prompt; Nexus never reads or fetches the URI.

AcpSessionInfoUpdate.description: The verification carrier: no field of its own, the object under `_meta`.

AcpStopReason.description: `refusal` exists in the specification and is never sent: a gate denial is a failed tool call inside a turn that continues.

AcpToolDiffContent.description: `path` is absolute. `oldText` is null for a new file. One block per hunk: the text is the hunk's lines, not the whole file.

AcpToolKind.description: The tool kinds of the specification that Nexus uses; `move` and `switch_mode` exist there and no Nexus tool is one.

AcpToolRawInput.description: The tool's name and subject as the sidecar reported them (already redacted and bounded).

denied.description: The operator declined the call at its approval prompt; it did not run.

AcpUserMessageChunk.description: Sent only while replaying a loaded session.

AcpValidationReceipt.description: The validation receipt of an authoritative verifier run, as the receipt's "Validation receipt" section shows it.

AcpVerification.description:
What Nexus can demonstrate about a turn. `end_turn` says nothing about verification; this object does.
`receipt_id`: the validation receipt id when one is active, else `turn:<sessionId>:<turnId>`. `turn_id` is null only
for the last outcome of a loaded session, whose turn id the session record does not carry.

AcpVerifierRun.description: One verifier run of the turn.

AcpVerifyParams.description: The caller identifies an active session only; all verification authority belongs to the server operator.

EngineeringOutcome.description:
VERIFIED        - the verifier selected for this workspace ran and passed against the current changes
UNVERIFIED      - work ended with a result that was not (or could not be) verified; see reason. Either changes
                  no passing verifier covers, or an answer resting on tool output that context compaction removed
                  during the turn and the model did not re-read (CONTEXT_EVIDENCE_NOT_RETAINED)
NOT_ESTABLISHED - no engineering result was established (turn did not complete, or verifier failed)
NOT_REQUIRED    - the turn made no workspace change and every tool output it relied on was still in context

NexusReceipt.description: Result of `_nexus/receipt/get`. Nexus's own type, not part of the specification. Kept in memory for the process only.

NexusVerificationReceipt.description: Receipt of a workspace verification requested over ACP. Its result is the existing `nexus verify` v3 document.

NexusVerifyResult.description: Small result returned from `_nexus/verify`; the full verification result lives in its receipt.

base_pinned_commit.description: The commit the change was measured from, and when this process pinned it for the workspace.

workspace.description: What was verified: the canonical path of the session's directory, as in the receipt.

note.description: Why the section is empty, or a footnote.

operation.description: Code-defined label for the refused operation: `verify`, a tool name, or a worker.

reason.description: Short, control-character-free reason from the refusing code path.

SandboxEventEngine.description:
VR-3: the profile-agnostic shape of a sandbox refusal. A denial is evidence for a receipt and a flight record; it is
never an approval and never raises a verdict. `profile` is the named SB-1 profile the session was started with
(`:workspace`, `:read-only`, `:network`) and `"default"` when none was named (a refusal from `verify`, or a session
that set only the legacy flags), so the shape did not have to change when those names arrived.

errorCount.description: Located errors on the base; present when the base run can serve as a baseline.

status.description: NOT_RUN: discovery already ruled the project out (skipped, or its tool is missing).

baselineErrorCount.description: Errors the baseline run (before the change) already had.

enforced.description: False when the result is recorded only (operator-configured verifier, or NEXUS_TYPECHECK mode "record").

excerpt.description: Redacted, control characters made visible, capped, and fenced as untrusted compiler output.

introducedCount.description: Errors in the run that the pre-change baseline run did not have (present only when a baseline was captured).

projects.description: Per-project evidence when a workspace contains multiple configured type-check projects.

scope.description: What the result holds for: "under <configPath>", never universal.

shellChangedFiles.description: Files counted as modified that no edit tool touched (changed through the shell), when any.

status.description:
ENVIRONMENT: the check could not run or be attributed here (not a candidate failure). PREEXISTING: errors exist, but
none in a file the candidate modified; it is not a pass and does not block.

toolSha256.description: Hash of the resolved tool launcher.

command.description: The verifier actually selected: configured override or one discovered from repository files.

deadlineSecs.description: Deadline the verifier was given, recorded when it timed out.

definitionBound.description:
False when the verifier's inputs could not be bound to the tree that was committed: either its workspace-resolved
definition was unbindable (for example a node_modules tree under `npm test`) or test files changed while it ran
(including a test that restored itself before exit). No such pass can be independent evidence; the turn is then at
most REGRESSION_FREE, and independenceDetail names which binding failed.

filtered.description: True when the selected test command includes a filter and therefore cannot stand for the full suite.

independent.description:
A discovered verifier's pass is independent evidence of the change: tests that existed before it, unmodified,
failed before and pass after. False (with independenceDetail) when only the agent's own tests, or tests that also
passed before, check it — the turn is then REGRESSION_FREE, not VERIFIED.

typecheck.description: Type-check run beside the verifier. A scoped fact about the named configuration, never about the code in general.

failed.description: The verifier failed on the base tree.

testFiles.description: Test files captured from the base tree; null when one was too large to capture.

usable.description: The base run can serve as the "failed before" half: it failed, by itself, with tests that ran.

verifierDefinitionBound.description: The files that define the verifier were captured from the base tree.

verifierUnbindableReason.description: Why they could not be captured.

VerifyGuard.description: The verification-file guard: which changed files define or weaken the verification, under the BASE tree's policy.

complete.description: False when a changed file could not be classified (unreadable, too large, or too many findings).

mode.description: `approve`: a finding that requires approval blocks until approved. `block`: it blocks, and approval is not accepted.

policySource.description: `base_tree`: the base tree's `.nexus-security.json` (it can only tighten). `default`: the base tree has none. The head's is never read.

status.description: NOT_RUN: verification stopped before the change was read. CLEAR: nothing waits for a decision. BLOCKED: a finding does, or the scan is incomplete.

VerifyGuardFinding.description: One changed file that decides how the change is verified.

approved.description: The operator approved this path. Approval lets the verdict be reported; it never makes the change VERIFIED.

requiresApproval.description: The edit needs `--approve-verification-edit <path>`: a verification configuration file, or a weakened test.

weakening.description: For a test file: what the edit removed (a heuristic over the text). Absent when nothing was detected.

VerifyIngredient.description: An ingredient of the verdict that this version does not run. Later versions add statuses and members.

VerifyJsonResult.description: Printed when verification reached a verdict, whatever the verdict. It is also the receipt.

base.description: Absent when the checkout was refused before anything was resolved.

changedFiles.description: Paths that differ between base and head (at most 200 are listed).

environment.description: Names (never values) of verdict-affecting environment variables that were set.

linkedDependencyDirs.description: Dependency directories of the caller's checkout that were linked into both scratch trees.

reason.description: Absent only when the verdict is VERIFIED.

runs.description: Every verifier process that ran, in order.

sandbox.description: Always written; absent only in a document from before `--sandbox` existed (nothing was sandboxed).

sandboxEvents.description: Sandbox refusals encountered in this run. Present only when one happened; a denial is evidence, never an approval.

schema_version.description: Version of this document's schema. Always the first member.

verification.description: The evidence the outcome was derived from.

timeoutSecs.description: Deadline of each verifier run, and of the type-checks of each side, in seconds.

VerifyReason.description: Why the verdict is not VERIFIED: the outcome ladder's reasons, and the ones only `nexus verify` gives.

VerifyReview.description:
The independent reviewer's result. `NOT_RUN` is honest when no head verifier ran, so nothing was reviewed;
`COMPLETE` publishes only the members this reviewer writes, using the vocabulary of the project's existing
`IndependentReviewVerdict` (ACCEPT/REJECT, observations, defects, unproven criteria and scope violations). Internal
members such as `boundaryReport`, `changeAssessment` and a defect's optional line are deliberately not published.
A REJECT can withhold VERIFIED but never raise a verdict: deterministic verifier evidence stays the authority for a
passing result.

executedTests.description: The output shows at least one test that ran.

exitCode.description: Null when the process was killed or never started.

outputTail.description: The end of the output of a run that did not pass: repository-controlled text, redacted and capped.

phase.description: `base_tests_on_head`: the test files as they were on the base, run against the head's code.

sandboxed.description: The process ran inside the sandbox named in `sandbox.engine`. Always written; absent only in a document from before `--sandbox` existed (the run was not sandboxed).

testFixtureReads.description: Test-oracle files or candidate-only workspace paths opened/observed more often than by the base run. Such a pass is not independent; paths can include test-support data, not only test files.

VerifySandbox.description:
How the processes `nexus verify` started on repository content were confined: the verifier on each side, the base's
tests against the head, and the type-checks. One answer for all of them: a run is never started outside a sandbox
that was requested.

engine.description: The engine every process ran in. `none`: no sandbox (not requested, or requested and unavailable, in which case nothing ran).

network.description: The confined processes could use the network (`--sandbox-network`). Always false when `engine` is `none`: an unconfined process has the caller's network, which this member does not describe.

requested.description: The operator explicitly selected a sandbox; the effective engine and run records also show default confinement.

commit.description: The commit; null for the working tree, which has none.

ref.description: What the operator named: a ref, or "(working tree)".

tree.description: The Git tree that was materialised and verified. For the working tree: tracked and untracked files that are not ignored, as `git add -A` would stage them (Nexus's own `.nexus` state left out).

VerifyTypecheck.description:
The project type-checks. The evidence of every project (tool, configuration, status, counts, tool hash) is in
`verification.typecheck.projects`; this is the summary and the base side.

baseline.description: The same projects on the base tree: what a "new" error on the head is measured against.

missingFromHead.description: Projects of the base tree that the head no longer has (tool and configuration path).

mode.description: `enforce`: a failing check lowers the verdict. `record`: recorded only (your own `--verifier`). `off`: disabled by NEXUS_TYPECHECK.

status.description:
NOT_RUN: the verifier did not pass on the head (or verification stopped earlier), so no type-check was run.
Otherwise the combined status of the head's projects, as in `verification.typecheck.status`.

VerifyVerdict.description:
VERIFIED: evidence independent of the change shows it. REGRESSION_FREE: the tests pass, which shows only that nothing
they cover broke. UNVERIFIED: nothing was established (see `outcome` and `reason`). BLOCKED: a person must decide
before anything is run or concluded.

approval.description: How it was approved: it is the operator's own command, `--yes`, a matching `--approve-verifier` digest, or not at all.

digest.description: sha256 of the command and the script body it resolves to in the base tree.

evidence.description: The base-tree file that justifies a discovered verifier, or "configured".

script.description: The script body the command resolves to in the base tree (capped), when there is one.

source.description: `configured`: the operator's `--verifier`. `discovered`: selected from the files of the base tree.
